rv.q: There’s not a false note in any of the performances or an ill-considered directorial stroke in Mosher’s clear-eyed approach to this first-rate revival.
Mr. Schreiber is such a complete actor that he has often thrown productions into imbalance, highlighting the inadequacy of the performances around him. That is not a problem here.
Performed by a sizzling ensemble led by Mark Strong, this is powerhouse theater that leaves you breathless.

There's impressive work from Anna Francolini's worldly Beatrice, while Ronan Raftery's charmingly effete Rodolpho proves an irresistible catch for the faun-like innocence of Leila Mimmack's Catherine.
Now Liev Schreiber, one of the few American star-level actors to return to the stage on a regular basis, sinks his teeth into this meaty steak of a character and has a regular feast.
A new revival of A View From the Bridge features what could be this season's most inspired piece of movie-star casting.
Mosher's keeping everything at a safe distance makes this A View from the Bridge one you'd best approach with binoculars.
Schreiber, Johansson and company have managed to make it a memorable one.

cn.t: Schreiber delivers a titanic performance in this searing revival of Miller's tragedy, with strong support from Johansson in her stage debut. Most critics praise the production, though one finds it less compelling.

vs.sum: A beautifully restored theater with a stunning Tiffany-inspired interior. The 2021 renovation transformed restroom facilities from among Broadway's worst to a model for the industry, with modern bathrooms on every public level.

acc.note: Elevator to Mezzanine, Balcony, and lower level restrooms. 7 wheelchair spaces across all levels.
